metadata.title: How VinIntel scores work
metadata.description: The transparent methodology behind VinIntel scores: Value Score, Gift Score, and Food Match. Learn how we calculate value for Romanian wines.
metadata.shortDescription: The transparent methodology behind VinIntel scores for Romanian wines.

Scores.title: How VinIntel scores work
Scores.intro: We believe evaluations should be clear and honest. Here is exactly what we measure, how each score is calculated, and why you can trust our recommendations.
Scores.scoresIntro: Each wine receives three scores from 0 to 100, so you can quickly judge its value, gifting appeal, and versatility at the table.
Scores.valueSummary: How strong the quality-to-price ratio is. This is the platform's primary score.
Scores.valueFactor1: Estimated intrinsic quality (Q): notes, validated medals, region, winery, and vintage
Scores.valueFactor2: Price efficiency against similar wines at that price (70 = the segment's typical level)
Scores.valueFactor3: A combination of 72% quality + 28% price efficiency, with a ceiling linked to actual Q
Scores.giftSummary: How safe and compelling the bottle is as a general gift choice.
Scores.giftFactor1: Estimated quality and confidence in the data
Scores.giftFactor2: Value Score as a secondary signal, not price as prestige
Scores.giftFactor3: Documented distinctive identity. Packaging is not evaluated.
Scores.foodSummary: How versatile the wine is at the table overall. It does not indicate compatibility with one specific dish.
Scores.foodFactor3: General style utility, with low confidence when facts are missing
Scores.scaleTitle: How to read the score scale

bands.overpriced: Too expensive for what it offers

Scores.confidenceTitle: Data confidence, separate from the score
Scores.confidenceP1: Value Score shows value at the current price, but it does not show how strong the supporting data is. We therefore calculate a separate confidence percentage (0-100%), displayed alongside the score and never merged into one number. A wine with limited data, such as no producer, region, variety, medals, or verified reviews, automatically receives lower confidence.
Scores.confidenceP2: Low confidence reduces the maximum possible score, regardless of the estimated quality calculation. A wine with insufficient data cannot reach 90+ simply because information is missing. Missing data is not a positive signal. When confidence falls below the provisional score threshold, the wine page labels the score as provisional.
Scores.confidenceDetail: Confidence increases with the number of reliable fields available: variety, region, winery, verified medals, critic scores, confirmed tasting notes, and freshness of the observed price. A manual score override in admin is always visible, justified, and audited separately. It is never silent.
Scores.verificationP1: For alcohol, acidity, sugar, and other technical data, we look for official producer sources. A technical sheet is the strongest source, while an official page or catalog may confirm a fact when it identifies the exact wine.
Scores.verificationP2: A value is marked Verified only when the source can be linked to the wine and, where relevant, the correct vintage. Retailer information does not automatically confirm laboratory data.
Scores.verificationP3: If the necessary evidence is not yet available, a value may remain visible in the catalog with the label Official source unconfirmed. Missing data remains missing, and fact verification is separate from score calculation.
Scores.indicatorsIntro: Alongside the three scores, we add signals that make choosing easier.
Scores.beginnerDescription: Highlights wines that are easy to appreciate, without difficult notes or aggressive tannins.
Scores.agingDescription: Estimates how many more years a wine may develop favorably under proper storage conditions.
Scores.overrateDescription: Flags wines whose price appears higher than their real value in the glass.
Scores.independence: Scores cannot be purchased. Wineries may claim their profile to correct factual data, but the methodology remains the same for every wine. Some shop links may be affiliate links, but this never influences scores.
Scores.faq1Answer: Value Score combines intrinsic quality (Q) with price efficiency. Q estimates how good the wine is without using price. Price efficiency measures its position against the typical level of its segment at that price. The final result is 72% Q + 28% price efficiency.
Scores.faq2Question: Are scores influenced by money or wineries?
Scores.faq2Answer: No. Scores are independent. Wineries may claim their profile to correct factual data such as price, vintage, and specifications, but they cannot buy or modify scores. The methodology is the same for every wine.
Scores.faq3Answer: We recalculate scores periodically as new prices, reviews, and vintages become available. Value history is retained to track changes over time.
Scores.faq4Question: What does a score below 50 mean?
Scores.faq4Answer: A score below 50 does not mean the wine is poor. It means that, at the current price, alternatives offer a better quality-to-price ratio. For some occasions, Gift Score and table versatility may matter more than Value Score.
Scores.faq5Question: Why can a wine with insufficient data not receive a very high score?
Scores.faq5Answer: Data confidence is calculated separately and limits the maximum possible score. A wine without a confirmed producer, region, variety, or medals automatically receives low confidence. Its score is capped, for example at a maximum of 69/100 for insufficient data, and marked provisional. Missing data can never produce an exceptional score.

metadata.title: Add a Romanian wine
metadata.description: Paste a link to a Romanian wine. VinIntel analyzes it, generates scores, and adds it to the community database after review.
metadata.ogDescription: Community flywheel: link, AI analysis, scores, and a reviewed wine page.

AddWine.title: Add a Romanian wine
AddWine.description: Paste the product link. We analyze the page and generate scores and explanations, then the VinIntel team verifies the wine before publication.
AddWine.placeholder: https://www.emag.ro/... or a Profitshare / winery link
AddWine.step1: 1. We check whether the wine already exists in the VinIntel database.
AddWine.step2: 2. We extract factual data from the source page.
AddWine.step3: 3. We generate editorial analysis and Value / Gift / Food scores.
AddWine.step4: 4. The wine is submitted for verification and appears on the site after approval.
